common_name: Blue Jean Baby Russian Sage (Compact Early-Blooming Dwarf Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in lean, very well-drained soil in full sun; this patented Walters Gardens selection (PP29281) blooms earlier than most Russian sage cultivars and was bred to replace older dwarf selections with a more vigorous, floriferous habit.

directions: Blue Jean Baby forms a dense, well-branched mound of fragrant gray-green foliage topped by multiple upright spikes of lavender-blue flowers held in smoky purple calyxes, opening earlier in the season than standard Russian sage and continuing into fall. Its compact, self-supporting habit stays tidy without the floppy, woody sprawl of older seed-grown Russian sage, making it a good fit for smaller borders and mixed containers. Plant in average to dry, sharply drained soil in full sun; wet feet or heavy clay quickly lead to crown rot. Cut the whole plant back hard to a low framework in early spring once new basal growth appears, since flowers form on new wood.

common_name: CrazyBlue Russian Sage (Very Compact Dwarf Russian Sage)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in lean, very well-drained soil in full sun; this patented Walters Gardens selection (PP25,639) is among the most dwarf Russian sage cultivars available, staying well under half the height of the species.

directions: CrazyBlue is an exceptionally compact Russian sage that forms a dense, stiffly upright mound of aromatic silvery gray-green foliage only about a foot tall, topped from summer into fall with violet-blue flower spikes set in smoky purple calyxes. Its small stature and rigid stems mean it holds its shape in the front of a border or in a container without the staking or flopping that taller Russian sage cultivars can need. Grow in average to dry, sharply drained soil in full sun, since wet or heavy soils invite crown rot. Cut the plant back nearly to the ground in late winter before new growth resumes to keep the mound dense and compact.
